# SPARSE35: weaknesses, proposals and decisions (synthesis, 2026-10-04)

**Bottom line.** No model-side training arm survives at >= +0.01 on roi303. The only measured positive effect is an instancer change (RELINK, roughly +0.01 roi303 / +0.02 htw on VAL), which needs two rulings from you. The largest model-owned row, htw detection (+0.113 on VAL), has no surviving attack. The rest of the movement in the reported number sits in your benchmark decisions.

## 1. Which numbers, and the split defect

- **Declared numbers:** roi303 TEST (137 frames) 0.641 +- 0.006 and htw TEST (33 frames) 0.601 +- 0.012. Three seeds, ep040, centerline-F1 at tol 5, coverage 0.80/0.80, pooled micro, min_length 15, threshold from each block's own VAL. The blocks are never pooled.
- **Split defect:** `roi_img_208` (VAL) and `209` (TEST) are byte-identical, as are 172=173 (both TEST) and 206=207 (both VAL). About 94 sibling pairs cross the split (`docs/TODO.md:2702-2710`).
- **How proposals are read:** paired on roi303 VAL and htw VAL. TEST is read once, after the re-split by field.
- **Anatomy is VAL only.** TEST has counts but no FP/FN classes, and no TEST dump was re-read today.
- **Frame counts disagree and must be reconciled before any re-split:** tulen RAW has 281 frames (141/140), the sweep rows cover 276 (139 + 137), the local 8-bit export has 277 (139/138).
- **The +-0.006 is training-seed sd, not a confidence interval.** A refuter measured the roi303 TEST 95 % half-width at about +-0.040 (frame bootstrap) and +-0.050 (group bootstrap).

- **In-domain claims about curves under 15 px are unmeasured.** The synth eval set was built with `--min-len 15`, and 15.5 % of htw GT is under 12 px.

New facts from today's lanes (exploratory, VAL only, one model seed unless stated):

- **`w_ori` is inert on the binary head.** The instancer runs geometry-only at junctions.
- **Close parallels remain unsolved:** bundle recovery is 67/266 (25 %) on roi303 and nothing moved it.

Notes on RELINK:
- **The effect is real on a bit-identical map.** `w_theta` x2 gives roi303 VAL +0.0188 (p 0.0016) and htw +0.0243 (p 0.0027), replicated on three seeds. Synth exact GT agrees in sign (+0.045).
- **Refuter 1's objection is procedural.** Real VAL was read before synth and shaped the frozen set, and the earning rule was written after the numbers were seen.
- **Refuter 2 corrected the mechanism.** On htw all 27 recovered curves were covered by one over-long prediction that was itself an FP. The event is "1 FP + 1 FN -> 1 TP + 1 FP", not a chimera split.
- **The gain is recall only.** Precision is flat, FP rises (+61 on roi303), junction identity moves 829 -> 819 of 2043, bundle recovery 67 -> 65 of 266. It is not a crossing or parallel fix.
- **Over-restriction turns negative on roi303** (-0.008 on a 28-frame subset) while synth still reads +0.027. That is why the selection rule is the smallest multiplier on the synth plateau.
- **The htw plateau is flat and robust** (+0.024 to +0.030 across all restrictive variants). The roi303 side is the fragile one.

## 5. Refuted today (so they are not rediscovered)

The 101-row closure ledger in the digest stands. Today's kills:

Judged proposals:
- **DECODE-ORDER, variant (b)** (threshold at native, then zoom the mask): measured null. htw -0.005 at own threshold on all 33 frames; roi303 +0.002 on a 53-frame subset. **CONTESTED for variant (c) and tile fusion:** the FATAL verdict was called without running either, and 8.5 % of on-filament native support on htw is erased by the resample.

More saturated curves are missed less (0.309 / 0.181 / 0.096 by tercile). Caveat from the critic: n = 33 frames in two clusters, pseudo-replicated p-values.
- **ENCPROBE / VFMSKIP** (frozen foundation encoder): premise contradicted (DINOv2 features separate synth from real at ~0.98, no better than the trunk's 0.95); the probe's kill line is void because its populations are selected on SPARSE35's own output.
- **RELINK-D as a 7-dim Optuna:** superseded by the 1-D version; a joint synth optimum can overshoot.
- **Decision B option B1 as written:** the outcome depends on the correlation threshold (-0.006 at 0.99, -0.03 to -0.06 at 0.95).

Ordering lane:
- **Spatially heteroscedastic noise:** synth is already more heterogeneous than real (MAD-CV 0.120 vs 0.052).
- **Clutter co-location:** AUC 0.51-0.57 against a 0.60 kill line.

- **Length-normalised loss:** equated with WORSTPOINT, which floods htw (miss 0.310 -> 0.502 / 0.692 at matched off-annotation foreground). **Soft kill:** blob loss is a different redistribution, and the dumps were trainer picks, not ep040.
- **Ranking / AP loss, PASTA, RandConv, GIN, distractors, MixStyle, flat-minima optimisers:** in-domain AP 0.996 leaves no mis-ordered pairs, or the class is AUG_PHOTO / ARM 41.

- **Skeleton Recall, CoLeTra dropout:** reduce to pos_weight or a refuted premise (render dips already in the real range).
- **Tip restoration before min_length:** retraction is only 0.5-1.8 px; returns about 25 htw curves on a perfect map.
- **Along-filament integration:** closed on roi303 (recall 0.04-0.05 vs kill line 0.20). **Alive on htw:** 0.36-0.40, on 287 weak samples of long filaments; ceiling about +0.02-0.03.

- **Orientation side-channel, frozen-trunk K=6 head, double-angle regression:** equal `w_theta` x2 within 0.002; the trained AMODAL channels give only +0.009 / +0.004.
- **Shorter link range:** x0.5 is -0.029 on roi303; link off is -0.128.
- **CondInst, curve queries, geodesic tracking, gap-weighted loss for parallels:** prize is <= 0.03 roi303 and 0 on htw.

Generator and encoder lanes:

- **SSL pretraining, ResEnc-L/XL, DINOv3 trunk, SAM fine-tune, normalisation randomisation:** no clean data, not capacity-bound, or expected <= 0.005.

Benchmark lane:
- **Ignore rule on weak annotated stretches, model-derived ignore band, shorter-curve exclusion, length-weighted primary, looser tolerance:** each fits the convention to a model failure or changes the instrument after TEST was read.

## 7. Recommended order of work

**Step 1, CPU only, cached dumps (about a day):**
1. Reconcile the roi303 frame counts (281 / 277 / 276).
2. Run `diag_fp_anatomy.py` on the `w_theta` x2 dump. This settles RELINK's label and its mechanism gate.
3. Re-read the cached arms under the declared metric, SCALE and SCALE_S2 on htw first, then NOISE, COMBO, TIRF 0/20/35/50.
4. Read FWHM against miss within each htw saturation cluster.
5. Check the oracle's 121 perfect-band misses on htw against per-curve length.
6. Build the htw off-annotation montage (the +0.072 row was never classified).
7. Paired frame and group bootstrap of ARM 50-55 and PAINT_AA on cached per-frame rows.
8. Rebuild the synth eval set with min-len 5 and re-read the length-binned miss.

**Step 2, under 0.3 GPU-h, needs your go:** one native logit re-dump of SPARSE35 ep040 on roi303 VAL and htw VAL. It reads tile fusion, decode variant (c), and weak-point share against tile-edge distance in one pass.

**Step 3, gated arms:**
- **Width/scale-support arm (2 seeds):** only if the SCALE htw re-read and the within-cluster FWHM read both point out of support.
- **PAINT_AA seed 2 (~6 GPU-h):** justified as a defect fix; it earns a recipe place only if roi303 replicates and htw does not fall.
- **RELINK 1-D (0 GPU-h):** only on your ruling, and only if step 1.2 shows over-long single-prediction FN falling with total FP up by no more than about 3 %.
- **Tile-fusion change:** only if step 2 moves micro beyond +0.006 roi303 or +0.012 htw at each variant's own threshold, and you rule it a defect fix.

**Step 4, before any TEST read:** dedupe, fix the group definition, re-declare, then read TEST once per seed.

For a ridge whose above-threshold support at native is about 1 px wide, bilinear interpolation between the peak pixel and its sub-threshold neighbours pushes most eval-frame pixels under the threshold. The result is a width-dependent effective threshold: fat-topped blobs pass unchanged, thin marginal filaments are chopped or erased. That is an ordering distortion in exactly the direction the digest names (weak filament stretches lose to off-annotation blobs), and it exists only on real data because in domain the ridge has a flat 2-3 px top. The chopped pieces are then deleted, not bridged: instance_a drops chains shorter than min_length*0.5 = 7.5 px BEFORE the free-end linker runs (src/instance/instancer_a.py:364). I ran the declared instancer end to end on a toy ridge (300 eval px, random angle, Gaussian logit cross-profile, params_a_derived.json; script in the scratchpad, CPU only). Share of the ridge length returned as (a) declared / (b) threshold at native then nearest-neighbour zoom of the mask / (c) resample logits: thr 0.98, peak 1.0 logit above threshold, sigma 1.2 px: 0.00 / 1.01 / 0.37; peak 2.5 logits above (p 0.998), sigma 1.2: 0.57 / 1.01 / 1.00; sigma 0.8: 0.00 / 1.01 / 0.97. At thr 0.995: margin 2.5, sigma 1.2: 0.28 / 1.01 / 1.00; margin 1.0, sigma 1.2: 0.00 / 0.99 / 0.02. So a filament the network holds at p 0.998 along its whole length can be returned at half length or not at all under the declared path. The toy says nothing about how many real filaments sit in that regime; ledger facts that say it is common on real and absent in domain: per-curve minimum probability 0.54-0.87 on real vs 0.94 in domain (TODO.md:3762-3771), 'at the optimum the mask is thin and fragments +15 %' (TODO.md:2661), mask gap at cuts q50 = 1 px (TODO.md:1198). The second factor read from the same re-dump is tile fusion: predict() averages overlapping tiles uniformly in probability space with 24 % overlap (train_v5.py:926-958); at a 0.98 threshold a probability average behaves like an AND of the two passes (0.999 and 0.90 average to 0.95 and fail; averaged as logits they give 0.989 and pass), and 70 % of pixels are multi-pass (worklog.md:1930-1946).

proposal.title: ENCPROBE: frozen-feature ordering probe on real pixels, gating one frozen-encoder fusion arm (VFMSKIP)
proposal.anatomy_item: roi303: 'weak plain stretches on annotated filaments' (model-owned ordering, ~0.07-0.08, convention share unresolved). htw: 'Detection of annotated filaments' (+0.113 on VAL; missed curves are short, visible, carried at p >= 0.5 in 78 % of cases, lost to ordering against off-annotation blobs).
proposal.price_ceiling: roi303 VAL micro: 0.07-0.08 for the whole row; the ordering share an encoder can reach is capped here at +0.02. htw: +0.113 is the perfect-map ceiling on VAL; capped here at +0.03. htw TEST carries 45 % more FP than VAL, so VAL gains will not transfer in full.
proposal.mechanism: The ResEnc-M trunk is trained from scratch on renders only, and its own 32-channel representation separates render from real at 0.95 linear accuracy (TODO:4243-4266); on real it ranks faint on-filament pixels below off-annotation blobs although it sees them (weak stretches: median p 0.89, AUC 0.95 vs displaced background). A frozen encoder pretrained on real images cannot drift toward render-specific cues during synthetic training, which is the mechanism Rein reports for synthetic-to-real segmentation (frozen > fully fine-tuned, arXiv 2312.04265). Whether that holds for 2-3 px filaments in IRM is an open empirical question with published counter-evidence (arXiv 2509.06467, 2602.08505), which is why the probe decides before anything is built. Two axes on which this differs from the v4b hybrid: (a) resolution - candidates are read at an effective stride of <= 4 native px (hierarchical early stages, or ViT on 2-4x upsampled crops) and the nnU-Net full-resolution path is kept intact instead of being replaced; (b) the encoder is chosen by measured real ordering, not assumed.
proposal.what_changes: STAGE 0 (pre-screen only, see prescreen). STAGE 1, only on a pass: scripts/train_v5.py, build_model (:169-185) gains `--arch nnunet_vfm --vfm <winner>`: the unchanged ResEnc-M (NNUNET_PLAN :139-146) plus the frozen winner's features injected into the decoder skips at strides 4/8/16 through 1x1 projections with a zero-initialised gate, so step 0 is exactly SPARSE35's function and the dense path cannot lose resolution. Everything else is the SPARSE35 launcher line (scripts/run_sparse_sweep.sh: calib_V6_c070_narrow.json, --tirf-prob 0.35 --tirf-label-sparse, 40 x 6000, batch 8, ep040). Arms: VFMSKIP x 2 seeds + VFMSKIP_RAND (same fusion, randomly initialised frozen encoder of the same shape) as the regularisation control required by trap 5 (an auxiliary pathway helps even with a scrambled target, OVERLAP_SCRAM). - DRIVE (Staal et al. 2004, cited via CorpusId 285027095 and 234355865): a FOV mask per image, evaluation only inside it; observers marked pixels 'at least 70 % certain'; test images carry two manual segmentations, the first is ground truth, the second is the human reference (12.7 % vs 12.3 % vessel pixels on DRIVE, 10.4 % vs 14.9 % on STARE - observers differ by up to 40 % in how much they draw). Limitation: pixel metrics, not instances.
- SynthMT, Koddenbrock et al., PLoS Comput Biol 2026, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013901 (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.01.09.698597) - the source of htw: 66 real IRM frames, two independent annotators, one designated GT and the other scored as a prediction: human SKIoU 0.80 +- 0.14; SAM3Text + HPO 0.74 +- 0.18 is called 'human-grade'. Limitation: SKIoU, not our centerline F1; crops from 44 videos.
- Barz & Denzler, J. Imaging 2020, DOI 10.3390/jimaging6060041 / arXiv 1902.00423: 3.3 % (CIFAR-10) and 10 % (CIFAR-100) of test images have near-duplicates in train; replacing them (ciFAIR) and re-evaluating is the accepted repair; they report a 9-14 % relative accuracy drop on the duplicate-free test set. Its 2026 citing papers are mostly dataset audits that adopt sequence/session-level splits (e.g. DOI 10.3390/technologies14090531, arXiv 2609.01786, arXiv 2610.00421).

- Filament-tracing practice (FiNTA, Flormann et al., DOI 10.1096/fj.202100048R; Zhang et al., MBoC 2017, PMC5231901): accuracy is reported against a manual trace of the same image with FP/FN as length or count shares; none handles incomplete manual traces - there is no field standard to appeal to, so an explicit, model-blind protocol is defensible and necessary.

(ii) The re-split by acquisition group will not move the score but will widen the honest uncertainty, and it has to happen before a TEST number is printed. (iii) The 'evidence-free bridged stretches ~0.07' row must NOT be touched by any ignore rule: the digest re-labelled it as model-owned ordering (network AUC 0.95 on those stretches), so relaxing the metric there would be fitting the convention to a model failure.

proposal.title: DECISION A - model-blind annotation-completion pass on a pre-declared sample, with ignore regions and a second annotator (exhaustiveness-audited secondary score + human reference row)
proposal.anatomy_item: roi303: 'unannotated real filaments + short bright rods/seeds (on_gt < 0.10, not edge)', price ~0.05 (0.045-0.057), inside the off-annotation total +0.091 (hw 2.0). htw: off-annotation foreground +0.072 on VAL (ownership unresolved; TEST carries 45 % more FP so the row is probably larger there). NOT targeted: field-stop edge (~0.02, generator-owned, ARM 50), particles, and the weak-stretch row (~0.07, model-owned ordering).
proposal.mechanism: The declared metric charges an FP for every prediction that follows a real filament the annotator did not draw. Whether that row is the benchmark's or the model's is the one load-bearing unknown of the whole anatomy (roi303 confidence 'medium', htw 'low', no montage or classifier was ever run on htw). The only model-free way to price it is a human pass that never sees a prediction: on a pre-declared random sample the annotator (1) adds every filament they judge visible, (2) draws IGNORE polygons over zones they cannot or will not resolve (aperture exterior, saturated borders, debris clusters, unresolvable bundles), (3) sets a per-frame flag 'exhaustive yes/no'. A second annotator repeats this independently on the same frames. Scoring then has three honest outputs: the as-annotated score (unchanged, stays in the paper), the completed-GT score on the audited subset (added curves are GT, so they can also become FN; predictions with >= 50 % of their skeleton inside an ignore polygon are neither TP nor FP, ignore GT is not an FN), and the annotator-vs-annotator score under the same metric as the human reference. This is LVIS's exhaustiveness flag plus Caltech-style ignore regions plus the DRIVE/SynthMT second-observer row, applied to curves.
proposal.what_changes: No model, generator or training change. (1) Declaration file written BEFORE any annotation, next to docs/roi303_split.json: sample drawn by seeded shuffle stratified by density tercile x acquisition group, proposed 12 roi303 VAL + 24 roi303 TEST + 12 htw VAL + 12 htw TEST frames; the annotation instruction text (DRIVE-style certainty rule, e.g. 'draw a filament if you are at least 70 % certain and it is >= 10 native px long'); the rule for ignore regions; which of the three scores is primary. (2) Annotation in CVAT (cvat.utia.cas.cz) on the RAW frames with the EXISTING polylines visible and NO model overlay; new polylines get attribute source='completion', polygons label 'ignore'. (3) src/instance/metrics.py: add an optional `ignore_mask` argument to `centerline_f1` (default None = bit-identical): before the Hungarian step drop predictions whose skeleton lies >= 50 % inside the mask, and exclude GT samples inside the mask from coverage; add regression tests in tests/test_metrics.py (default path bit-identical, ignore prediction is neither TP nor FP, ignore GT is not FN). (4) scripts/eval_v5.py: flag `--gt-variant {as_annotated,completed}` and `--ignore` reading the polygons from the h5; scripts/build_roi_dataset.py stores `completion` polylines in a separate dataset so the as-annotated GT stays byte-identical. (5) Re-score the cached ep040 dumps of the three seeds (SPARSE35, SEED2, SEED3) on the audited subset, threshold from the block's own VAL exactly as declared. Recommended ruling to offer the user: as-annotated stays PRIMARY (0.641 / 0.601); the completed-subset score and the human reference are a pre-declared SECONDARY table. (3) 0.0-TIRFPERF 'recall over bright samples' (TODO:5986-5995) - an ignore rule derived from image brightness inside a curve; here nothing is derived from the image or the model. leads.code_findings:
Scope read end to end: scripts/train_v5.py, scripts/eval_v5.py, synth/mt_generator.py, src/instance/instancer_a.py, skeleton_graph.py, metrics.py (centerline_f1 / aggregate), matching.py (header + cost), the launchers scripts/run_arm.sh and run_sparse_sweep.sh, calib_V6_c070_narrow.json / calib_V6_noise.json, params_a_derived.json. Two findings were checked by local CPU simulation (geometry only, no training, nothing written to the repo). Ordered by how much they could matter.

1. DEAD PARAMETER - IRM filaments have no along-length intensity modulation. `along_intensity_std` (synth/mt_generator.py:139) is consumed by `_along_intensity` (:430-436), which is called ONLY in render_tirf (:770). render_irm builds `mod = c * _tip_taper(n, rng, cfg)` (:739) and never calls it. With the SPARSE35 calib (height_clamp_to_regime true, height_along_std_nm 6.0) the only along-filament variation left in IRM is a +-6 nm height walk and the tip taper. This is the code-level reason for docs/TODO.md:3772 'the generator has never produced a filament with a locally weak point' (in-domain per-curve p_min flat at 0.94 for every length). The ledger never records it as a dead parameter. Caveat: the lane it would feed was closed on a pre-screen (TODO:2722-2728, real weak stretches carry no image evidence), so this is a recorded-wrong-reason item, not a proven lever.

2. DECODE ORDER on the declared path: probabilities are bilinearly resampled x1.5 and THEN thresholded at 0.97-0.99. scripts/eval_v5.py:48-63 (`zoom(c, f, order=1)`), :217-219, :254; inference at native scale by train_v5.py:926-958. Toy check (ridge with a Gaussian logit cross-profile, thr 0.98): when the above-threshold support at native is <= 1 px wide (peak p ~0.99), a native-CONNECTED ridge of 300 px becomes 52-130 components after the resample at 10-30 deg, and can vanish entirely at 0/90 deg depending on sub-pixel row phase; with a flat 2-3 px top there is zero effect (in-domain-like profile: 0 change at every angle). So it bites only marginal real filaments - the same population that decides recall - and not in domain, which is why an in-domain check would never see it. Supporting ledger facts: 'at the optimum (0.99) the mask is thin and fragments +15 %' (TODO:2661), mask gap at cuts q50 1 px (TODO:1198). I do NOT claim this explains the grid anisotropy of the rotation probe: in my toy the angular pattern does not match the measured axis-aligned weakness. It is a property of the declared path (the SpheroSeg wrapper reproduces it to 2e-4, TODO:2668), not a coding slip. Settle without training: on one native re-dump, compare (a) declared, (b) threshold at native then zoom(mask, 1.5, order=0), (c) resample LOGITS; read skeleton endpoints per GT and micro F1 on roi303 VAL at each variant's own threshold. Whether (b)/(c) count as a fix or as a forbidden inference change is the user's ruling.

3. TILING: scripts/train_v5.py:926-958 averages overlapping tiles UNIFORMLY in probability space, stride round(512*392/518) = 387 (24 % overlap), no Gaussian weighting, with per-tile InstanceNorm statistics (build_nnunet :163, norm_op InstanceNorm2d). At a 0.98 threshold a probability average behaves close to an AND of the two passes (0.999 and 0.90 average to 0.95 and fail; the same pair averaged as logits gives 0.989 and passes), so the weaker tile - the one seeing the pixel near its zero-padded edge - decides. worklog.md:1930-1946 already measured that 70 % of pixels are multi-pass averages and that tile intensity SD varies 8.3x; no F1 read followed (see lead 'CONTEXT'). Training never sees more than a 640 px scene (train_v5.py:402; main() at :1253 never passes `gen`).

4. BORDER LABEL SMEAR in the synthetic loader. `ori_channels_soft` clips out-of-frame centerline samples onto the border (train_v5.py:261-262; same in heat_channel :209-210), while the renderer drops them (`ok` mask, mt_generator.py:550). RealDS explicitly guards against exactly this ('a curve leaving the crop would be smeared along its edge and taught as foreground that is not there', train_v5.py:592-608); OnlineDS has no such guard. Simulated with the SPARSE35 morphology overrides (300 scenes x 20 crops): 34.5 % of sampled centerline length lies OUTSIDE the 640 render (start is uniform in-frame, mt_generator.py:286-287), 99 % of renders carry smeared border labels, but only 4.9 % of 512-of-640 crops include any, = 0.08 % of target foreground pixels (1.7 % of foreground in border-touching crops). Verdict: real but latent at the shipped recipe - not a lever. It goes live if crop approaches the render size or scale-aug shrinks the frame (--scale-aug 0.8 makes a 512 px frame = the crop, so the SCALE / COMBO arms trained with it on a share of batches). By-product: a third of every generated filament is computed and thrown away.

5. NORMALISATION SUPPORT, and a wrong number in the docs. Training stretches [1,99] percentiles over the whole 640 px render then crops 512 (train_v5.py:497-498, :502-510); evaluation stretches the whole 730-2048 px real frame (eval_v5.py:216, norm01 at train_v5.py:860-862). Known and read as null at 0.80/0.80 on roi303 VAL (TODO:4286-4310: +0.004 macro, -0.004 micro) although real in the map (max |dp| 1.0, foreground nearly doubles). The read used --norm-support 768, and eval_v5.py:69 and TODO:4306 both say 'a 768 render'; the code default is gen=640 (TODO:1591 has it right). The null stands; the documented support is wrong. Only the inference side was tested - a training-side fix (randomised support / no clip) never was.

6. INERT INSTANCER WEIGHT on the binary head. eval_v5.py:249 `ori = ch[:K_ORI]` yields a 1-channel array for a --head binary checkpoint; `_ori_profile` (instancer_a.py:113-124) then returns a 1-element vector and `_ori_mismatch` (matching.py:44-58) is 1 - cos of two positive scalars = 0 for every pair. So `w_ori` 2.60 in params_a_derived.json does nothing for SPARSE35, and arm 29's Optuna moved a dead parameter (2.60 -> 5.23, TODO:1617). Harmless to the score; it means the instancer runs geometry-only at junctions, and that one of the 14 'tuned' weights is noise.

7. GENERATOR NEVER RENDERS, real frames contain: (i) coarse grey-level quantisation - 44 of 141 roi303 VAL frames have < 300 grey levels, 16-50 in the worst, and coarse frames are MAP_BREAK-heavy at 52 % (TODO:246-247, :861-862); SPARSE35 trains with photo_aug 0 (train_v5.py:1155), and AUG_PHOTO bundled quantisation with five other nuisances (negative at native), so quantisation alone was never isolated; (ii) correlated / heavy-tailed noise (off in the shipped calib, see leads); (iii) a field stop (--fov-prob 0 in every launcher; ARM 50 negative); (iv) bundles above 3 filaments or gaps under 3 px (mt_generator.py:31-33); (v) density above ~54 curves/Mpx while roi303 frames above 80/Mpx hold 33 % of all GT and score 0.42 (TODO:248-249; DENSE arm null under the old metric).

8. REPRODUCIBILITY GAP in the data path. `build_cfg` is imported from `gen_train` at a hard-coded tulen path (train_v5.py:1193-1196; also sys.path at :49); gen_train.py is not in this repository (git ls-files has no match), so the mapping from calib `best_params` (density_center, contrast_center, psf_center, waviness_amp_center ...) to GenConfig ranges cannot be audited or reproduced from git. The actual width of the shipped priors lives in an unversioned file.

9. TRAINER VAL IS NOT THE DECLARED READ. validate() (train_v5.py:961-996) scores strict 0.95/0.95, at 1.5x network input (up=UP), at the params file's prob_thr (:1274), on the first --val-n frames of mt34_htw_eval (:1267-1272), with the gate fg <= 3*synth_fg (:1542). Under the ep040 rule the pick is unused, so no score is lost, but any 'VAL trace' quoted from a training log measures a different quantity (already a recorded trap; listed for completeness).

10. METRIC INSTRUMENT (not model, 'ported verbatim - do not change'): centerline_f1 assigns by Hungarian on 1 - pairF1 and only then applies the 0.80/0.80 test (metrics.py:152-172), so the assignment maximises summed pair-F1, not TP count, and can under-count when fragments compete for one GT; GT polylines are clipped onto the frame border when rasterised (:39-40).
